newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker, Jan hits new contract low.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker, Jan hits new contract low.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled sharply lower, with the front two contracts falling to lifetime lows during the session.
Spot-January hit a contract low of 96.50 and second-position March fell to 99.50.
The most-active January contract closed down 3.85 cent a lb at 97.15, having ranged from 101.20 to 96.50. The back months finished 3.70 to 3.50 lower.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 3,000 lots.
Dealers said speculative selling pushed prices lower early, and trade hedging kept pressure on the market.
Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with Paine Webber, noted that the weekly chart has been in a downtrend channel for more than six months, and pegged nearby support at 95.00 in January.
He said the contract could easily test the next levels of support at 92.40, 91.75, and 89.50.
Additionally, the failure of the January/March spread to maintain the tightness of November/January, signaled weaker prices.
"The accompanying Jan/March spread could have very bearish ramifications for the market, as it indicates that the tightness in November was not transferred," Savaiko said.
